data.name: Israel
data.summary: Israeli residents pay 25% on real capital gains on shares and on dividends (30% for 10%+ shareholders), plus a 3% surtax and, since 2025, an extra 2% surtax on capital income above ILS 721,560 (2026), so a large investor pays 30% on gains and dividends. There is no inheritance, estate, gift or wealth tax. New immigrants (olim) and senior returning residents after 10 years abroad are exempt for 10 years on foreign passive income and on gains from foreign assets; those arriving from 2026 must now report that exempt income. Immigration is open mainly to people eligible under the Law of Return.

regimes.name: Israeli tax resident
regimes.description: Worldwide income; fixed 25%/30% rates on capital gains and dividends plus surtax 3% + 2% on capital income above ILS 721,560.
regimes.eligibility: Centre of life in Israel; presumed with 183 days in a year, or 30 days in the year and 425 days over three years (rebuttable).

capital_gains.summary: Real (inflation-adjusted) gains on shares acquired from 2003 are taxed at 25%, or 30% for a substantial (10%+) shareholder. A 3% surtax applies to taxable income above ILS 721,560 (2026) and, from 2025, an additional 2% surtax on capital income (gains, dividends, interest, rent) above the same threshold: top rate 30% (35% for substantial shareholders).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Surtax threshold ILS 721,560 (2026). Inflation adjustment of the cost base (real gain).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Israeli real estate is taxed under the Land Appreciation Tax Law (real betterment accrued after 1 January 2012 taxed at up to 25%, 30% for a 10%+ holder of a real estate company; residential apartments: pre-2014 betterment exempt and a sole apartment can be fully exempt; purchase tax 6%, or 0-10% for a sole residential apartment (Deloitte 2026)). Exit tax provisions apply on ceasing residence (mechanics not verified in this session). Shares bought before 2003: blended rate.

sources.title: Israel - Individual - Taxes on personal income

capital_gains.rate_basis: Portfolio shares: 25% + 3% surtax + 2% capital-income surtax = 30% on the part above ILS 721,560. Private business (10%+ holder): 30% + 5% = 35%. Real estate: assumed 25% land appreciation/real gain rate + 5% surtax = 30% (LAT rate per Deloitte Highlights 2026). Real gains only (inflation-indexed cost).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains from business-like trading are ordinary income at marginal rates up to 47% + surtaxes.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None; real gain computed with CPI indexation.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide gains taxed with foreign tax credit; exit tax on emigration.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed at 25% (30% for a 10%+ shareholder) plus the 3% and 2% surtaxes on income above ILS 721,560: 30% at the top for portfolio holdings. Foreign dividends are taxed at the same rate with credit for foreign tax.
dividends.important_exceptions: Dividends from approved/preferred enterprises: 15-20%. Family companies: from 2025 a 2% annual tax on certain accumulated profits unless distributed.
dividends.rate_basis: 25% + 3% + 2% surtax = 30% for a portfolio investor whose income exceeds ILS 721,560.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 25% (30% for substantial shareholders) on dividends to non-residents, reduced by treaty.
dividends.treaty_network: About 60 treaties (PwC table), including the US (12.5%/15%/25%).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 23% (2026); distributions add 25-30% dividend tax. Closely held 'family' companies face income attribution and a 2% tax on accumulated profits from 2025. No holding structure is modelled: 23% company tax plus 25-30% dividend tax on payout (and surtax) exceeds the 30% top rate on direct holding, and the closely held company rules remove most of the deferral.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal tax (arnona) on occupiers of property. Purchase tax on real estate acquisitions (rates not verified).

inheritance.summary: No estate, inheritance or gift tax (inheritance tax abolished in 1981). Heirs inherit the deceased's cost basis, so gains are taxed when the heir sells. Gifts are generally exempt from income tax for the recipient, but the donee takes over the donor's cost and holding period.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Gifts of Israeli real estate can attract purchase tax at a reduced rate (one third for gifts to children; general knowledge, not verified). Inherited assets carry over the original cost, so embedded gains remain taxable on sale.
inheritance.gift_tax: None; donee inherits the donor's cost basis.

regimes.name: New immigrant (oleh) / senior returning resident - 10-year exemption
regimes.description: For 10 years from becoming resident, foreign passive income (dividends, interest, rent, pensions) and gains on foreign assets are exempt; gains on assets sold after the 10 years are apportioned. Residents from 1 January 2026 must report the exempt foreign income (the reporting exemption no longer applies). An optional first 'acclimation' year allows electing non-residence.
regimes.eligibility: New immigrant under the Law of Return (Jewish descent up to grandchildren, and spouses) or Israeli citizen returning after at least 10 consecutive years as a foreign resident (senior returning resident). Other foreigners cannot use it and generally cannot obtain residence.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on assets located abroad sold within the 10-year period are exempt; Israeli assets are taxed normally.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: New immigrant (oleh) or senior returning resident (10+ consecutive years abroad). Exemption runs 10 years from the date of immigration/return and covers foreign-source passive income and gains on assets located abroad; Israeli-source income and Israeli assets are taxed normally. Arrivals from 1 January 2026 must report the exempt foreign income (arrivals before 2026 remain exempt from reporting for the benefit period); the ITA may in any case demand a capital statement of Israeli assets.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: After 10 years, gains on foreign assets acquired before the end of the period are taxed on a time-apportioned (linear) basis. Arrivals from 1 January 2026 must report the exempt income. A foreign company managed by the new resident is generally not treated as Israeli-resident for 10 years (Deloitte), but the ITA may still assert a permanent establishment.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends exempt for 10 years; Israeli dividends taxed as standard.
dividends.eligibility_conditions: New immigrant (oleh) or senior returning resident (10+ consecutive years abroad). Exemption runs 10 years from the date of immigration/return and covers foreign-source passive income and gains on assets located abroad; Israeli-source income and Israeli assets are taxed normally. Arrivals from 1 January 2026 must report the exempt foreign income (arrivals before 2026 remain exempt from reporting for the benefit period); the ITA may in any case demand a capital statement of Israeli assets.
dividends.important_exceptions: Separate 2026 incentive (Deloitte): new immigrants and senior returning residents arriving between 5 November 2025 and 31 December 2026 get a tax holiday for 2026-2030 on income from personal activity in Israel (employment, business, profession) up to a ceiling (ILS 600,000 in 2026, ILS 1m in 2027 and 2028, ILS 350,000 in 2029, ILS 150,000 in 2030), conditional on staying resident and at least 75 days in Israel in 2028 and 2029. It does not cover passive investment income.

residency.tax_residency_test: Centre-of-life test; rebuttable presumptions at 183 days in the year, or 30 days in the year plus 425 days over the year and two prior years. New immigrants and returning residents after 10 years abroad have a 1-year acclimation period and may elect within 90 days not to be resident. Exit tax applies on ceasing residence.

corporate.summary: 23% CIT (2026); reduced rates for preferred enterprises/technology companies under the Encouragement of Capital Investments Law. QDMTT for groups with revenue of EUR 750 million or more from tax years beginning after 31 December 2025. From 2025, closely held companies face attribution of excess profits and a 2% tax on certain accumulated profits.

succession.name: Israel
succession.summary: There is no forced heirship: freedom of testation is a cornerstone of the Succession Law 1965. The court can, however, order maintenance from the estate for certain dependent relatives despite a will. Israel has a Trust Law 1979 and trusts are used, but private family foundations are not part of Israeli law.
succession.family_claims: Succession Law 5725-1965 s. 56 allows maintenance from the estate for certain relatives even where a valid will exists; s. 57 sets the scope, and s. 63 lets the court count certain pre-death transfers if the estate cannot meet the claims. Intestacy (no will): spouse gets household goods and half; the rest goes to the children.
succession.foreign_law_note: The law of the deceased's place of residence at death governs succession (Succession Law s. 138, with exceptions in ss. 139-140); a resident foreigner is therefore under Israeli law and a will cannot choose another law. Foreign probate orders are not recognised; an Israeli probate order is needed. Religious courts may apply community law on consent in some cases.
succession.trust_note: Trust Law 5739-1979 governs trusts; Israeli family trusts are mostly discretionary and irrevocable, often for minors. Foreign trusts are not covered by the Hague Convention here. Charitable bodies (amutot, public trusts) exist, but no statute for private family foundations was found, so 'limited'. Tax treatment of trusts (Income Tax Ordinance, Chapter on trusts) was not researched.
open_questions: Section 56 beneficiaries (which relatives qualify) were not retrieved; confirm against the statute text.
Whether a will can name foreign law for a foreign national domiciled in Israel (s. 138-140) is not confirmed.
No source on private foundations; charitable-only status is from general knowledge of amutot and needs a source.
Israeli trust tax rules (Income Tax Ordinance ss. 75B ff.) not researched.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.

immigration.name: Israel
immigration.summary: Israel has no investor or retirement residence and no digital nomad visa. People eligible under the Law of Return (Jews, their children, grandchildren and spouses) can immigrate and get citizenship on arrival, whatever their passport. Everyone else needs a sponsored work visa (B/1 for experts) or a family tie. EU, US and other passports are treated alike.
immigration.naturalisation: Permanent residents can apply after living in Israel 3 of the previous 5 years, with a settled life in Israel, some Hebrew, and renouncing other citizenship unless exempt (gov.il service page; minister's discretion). Law of Return immigrants get citizenship at once.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Israel allows its citizens to hold other citizenships. Naturalising foreigners are asked to renounce prior citizenship unless an exemption applies (gov.il).

routes.name: Aliyah under the Law of Return
routes.summary: Jews, their children and grandchildren and their spouses can immigrate to Israel and receive citizenship on arrival. No investment is needed.
routes.requirements: Law of Return 5710-1950 and its 1970 amendment (section 4A extends rights to a child and grandchild of a Jew and to their spouses). Persons born Jewish who converted to another religion are not eligible (secondary source); other exclusions in section 2(b) not read. The Ministry of Interior or Jewish Agency decides on proof of eligibility. Open to any passport; EU, US and OTHER all possible.
routes.physical_presence: Moving to Israel; Israeli tax residence follows the centre of life.
routes.tax_note: New immigrants have a tax acclimation period (see jurisdiction file); exit tax applies on leaving.

sources.title: Apply for Israeli citizenship according to section 4A of the Law of Return

routes.name: B/1 expert work visa
routes.summary: Employer-sponsored work visa for foreign experts; there is no route without an Israeli employer.
routes.requirements: The Israeli employer first obtains a permit from the Population and Immigration Authority, then the worker obtains the B/1 visa; employer must pay the statutory minimum salary and provide private medical insurance. From 1 January 2026 the minimum salary rose for applicants staying over three months or sponsored by Innovation Authority-recognised companies, and processing fees rose for all applicants (EY; amounts not in the sources read). Initial visa usually one year, extendable to about 63 months.
routes.physical_presence: Work and live in Israel for the employer.
routes.tax_note: Israeli residents are taxed on worldwide income; see jurisdiction file.
